findings.description: OPEN_IDS is built from `"$BR" list --json --limit 5000 2>/dev/null | jq ... || true`. Any failure of the tracker call (binary missing, DB locked, non-JSON output) or a tracker holding 5000+ issues yields an empty or truncated id list and records no problem. Under --apply, lines 183-184 then treat every closure id absent from OPEN_IDS as already closed, append an `already-closed` row to applied.jsonl, count it as skipped and exit 0 with 'applied 0 row(s), skipped N'. Because DONE_IDS (line 137) is read from that same log on the next run, those closures are never attempted again without hand-editing the append-only log. sweep-inventory.sh handles the identical call loudly (lines 54-58: exit on failure, exit when count reaches the limit); sweep-apply.sh does not.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: a concurrent session holds the beads DB lock while the lead runs --apply. br list fails, OPEN_IDS is empty, all 174 closure rows are logged already-closed, nothing is closed, exit 0 reports success. A re-run skips all 174 as already in applied.jsonl; the only record of mutations now asserts the tracker closed them before the sweep.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the br list exit status and the jq parse separately; on failure call `p "tracker list failed: ..."` so validation is INVALID and nothing mutates. Mirror sweep-inventory.sh's count-versus-limit check. Only write `already-closed` when the tracker list is known good.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: a concurrent session holds the beads DB lock while the lead runs --apply. br list fails, OPEN_IDS is empty, all 174 closure rows are logged already-closed, nothing is closed, exit 0 reports success. A re-run skips all 174 as already in applied.jsonl; the only record of mutations now asserts the tracker closed them before the sweep.

findings.description: A blocked closure is recognised only when `br close` returns non-zero AND its combined output contains 'blocked by'. The script never confirms the bead's status after a successful-looking close. The stub in tests/unit/sweep-tools.bats copies br's 'Warning: Skipped X: blocked by: Y' wording but invents an exit code of 3; if the real br emits that warning and exits 0 (it is phrased as a warning, not an error), `run` returns success, the row is logged `close`, the id enters DONE_IDS, and the bead stays open. No forced close occurs, but the applied log then asserts a closure that never happened and the re-run skips it. The test suite therefore proves the never-force property only against an assumed exit semantics.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: br close prints 'Warning: Skipped bd-x: blocked by: bd-kept' and exits 0. sweep-apply logs {action: close} for bd-x, reports it applied, and the re-run skips it. bd-x remains open with a log that says the sweep closed it; the next audit of the log cannot tell.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat output matching `Skipped|blocked by` as blocked regardless of exit status. After a close returns, verify with `"$BR" show "$id" --json` that status is closed before writing the `close` log row; otherwise log `close-unconfirmed` and count failed. Document br's actual exit behaviour and make the stub match it.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: br close prints 'Warning: Skipped bd-x: blocked by: bd-kept' and exits 0. sweep-apply logs {action: close} for bd-x, reports it applied, and the re-run skips it. bd-x remains open with a log that says the sweep closed it; the next audit of the log cannot tell.

findings.description: The 10 % re-verification (sweep-sample.sh --check) and the lead's triage are the stated controls that compensate for the permissive evidence resolver (DISS-C-007, accepted). Neither is mechanically required by --apply: the script looks for no sample file, no check receipt, and nothing binds a sample or verification file to the manifest set it validates (sample rows carry {id, category, evidence, batch} but no manifest-set hash, and --check never reads the manifests). Agent-produced closures can be applied without ever having been sampled, or after the manifests were rewritten following a passing check.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: the sample is drawn and checked against manifest-3 at 10:00; an agent batch rewrites manifest-3 at 10:20 with 40 closures evidenced by 'README.md'; the lead runs --apply at 10:30. Validation passes (path resolves), nothing notices the sample is stale, 40 beads close.
findings.suggested_fix: Have sweep-sample.sh --check write a receipt {manifests_sha256, sample_sha256, verified_sha256, result, ts}. Require `--sample-receipt FILE` for --apply and verify the manifests' sha matches; allow an explicit `--no-sample` override only if it is itself written into applied.jsonl. Embed the manifest-set sha in sample rows and check it in --check.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: the sample is drawn and checked against manifest-3 at 10:00; an agent batch rewrites manifest-3 at 10:20 with 40 closures evidenced by 'README.md'; the lead runs --apply at 10:30. Validation passes (path resolves), nothing notices the sample is stale, 40 beads close.

findings.description: Every mutation is performed first and logged second, with no write-ahead intent row, and `log_row` runs under set -e so a failed append (ENOSPC) aborts after the tracker already changed. DONE_IDS (line 137) is read with `jq -r '.id' ... || true`, so a log with a partial last line (crash mid-append) silently yields a partial id list, and the next append glues a new object onto the partial line, after which jq stops at that line and every later id vanishes from DONE_IDS. Closures stay safe via OPEN_IDS, but attribution is lost (a sweep-closed bead is re-logged `already-closed`), and kept/pulled-in rows get duplicate labels and comments. sweep-sample.sh --check fails closed on an unparseable file; sweep-apply.sh does not.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: the process is killed after `br close bd-a` succeeds and before log_row completes, leaving half a JSON object. On re-run jq reports bd-a's row unparseable, the || true hides it, bd-a is logged already-closed (false attribution), and the new row is appended to the broken line, making every subsequent log entry invisible to future idempotency checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Before trusting the log, require `jq -e -s 'all(.[]; type=="object" and (.id|type)=="string")' "$APPLIED"` and abort if it fails. Write an `intent` row before each mutation and a result row after. Check the last byte of the log is a newline (or empty) before appending.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: the process is killed after `br close bd-a` succeeds and before log_row completes, leaving half a JSON object. On re-run jq reports bd-a's row unparseable, the || true hides it, bd-a is logged already-closed (false attribution), and the new row is appended to the broken line, making every subsequent log entry invisible to future idempotency checks.

findings.description: inventory.jsonl and batches/*.jsonl freeze the first 2000 characters of every open bead's description, plus title and labels, into grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/sweep. The reviewer brief says the record branch carries a2a. The record branch's credential scan is pattern-based: it catches token-shaped strings but not internal hostnames, customer or partner names, or unreleased-plan text pasted into bead descriptions. If `.beads/` is already on the public record the exposure is unchanged; if it is not, this is a new bulk export of the whole open backlog's prose into a published directory.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: a bead description contains an internal staging hostname and a partner's name. The freeze copies it to a2a/sprint-275/sweep/inventory.jsonl and batches/batch-03.jsonl; the record branch script finds no credential pattern and publishes both.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm whether `.beads/` already reaches the record branch. If not, exclude `sweep/inventory.jsonl` and `sweep/batches/` from the record (keep inventory.sha256 and INVENTORY.md), or drop `description` from the frozen row and have Explore batches read it with `br show`.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: a bead description contains an internal staging hostname and a partner's name. The freeze copies it to a2a/sprint-275/sweep/inventory.jsonl and batches/batch-03.jsonl; the record branch script finds no credential pattern and publishes both.

findings.description: Evidence only has to match `\S`. A JSON escape such as `\u001b` decodes to a raw ESC byte; jq's @tsv escapes only tab, newline, CR and backslash, so ESC and other control bytes pass unchanged into `${ev:0:120}` echoed to the operator's terminal in the INVALID list (lines 142, 152), into the `--reason` text stored in the tracker (line 200-201), and into comments for kept rows. Agent-produced output can therefore emit terminal escape sequences into the lead's triage view, e.g. to clear or overwrite a preceding problem line.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: an agent writes evidence "\u001b[1A\u001b[2K ok" for an unresolvable closure. The INVALID listing prints the problem, then the escape sequence moves up and clears the line, hiding that bead's problem from a lead reading the terminal rather than the exit code.
findings.suggested_fix: In the jq field check reject evidence matching `test("[\\u0000-\\u001f\\u007f]")` and cap its length (for example 2000 chars). Optionally strip control characters before echoing with `tr -d '[:cntrl:]'`.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: an agent writes evidence "\u001b[1A\u001b[2K ok" for an unresolvable closure. The INVALID listing prints the problem, then the escape sequence moves up and clears the line, hiding that bead's problem from a lead reading the terminal rather than the exit code.

findings.description: `ROWS="$(mktemp)"` is safe, but the second file `$ROWS.ids` is a predictable name derived from it and is created at line 110 by a shell redirect, which follows symlinks. On a shared /tmp another local user who lists the directory after mktemp can plant a symlink at `<name>.ids` during the manifest-reading window and have the inventory id list written over an arbitrary file the operator can write.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: on a shared CI runner another job watches /tmp, sees tmp.AbC123 appear, creates tmp.AbC123.ids -> ~/.gitconfig; line 110 overwrites the operator's git config with bead ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `WORK="$(mktemp -d)"` and place both files inside it, or call mktemp a second time for the ids file.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: on a shared CI runner another job watches /tmp, sees tmp.AbC123 appear, creates tmp.AbC123.ids -> ~/.gitconfig; line 110 overwrites the operator's git config with bead ids.

findings.description: Refines DISS-C-007 rather than re-raising it. The path branch accepts any object `git cat-file -e HEAD:<ref>` can find, which includes trees: `.`, `./`, `src`, `.claude` and every directory name all resolve. A closure can therefore be evidenced by the repository root rather than by a file, which is weaker than the accepted design of 'a path that exists at HEAD'.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: an agent writes evidence "." for 30 closures. Validation prints VALID; the lead's triage sees a one-character path per row and has nothing to open; the 10 % sample happens to miss that batch; 30 beads close.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `[[ "$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" cat-file -t "HEAD:$ref" 2>/dev/null)" == blob ]]` and reject refs equal to `.` or starting with `./`.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: an agent writes evidence "." for 30 closures. Validation prints VALID; the lead's triage sees a one-character path per row and has nothing to open; the 10 % sample happens to miss that batch; 30 beads close.

findings.description: --check selects the first VERIFIED row per sampled id (`head -1`) and ignores any later row for the same id, so a disagreeing row that follows an agreeing one is never seen. The agree test compares the jq -r string output to `true`, so the JSON string "true" also passes. VERIFIED is agent-produced, which is exactly the file this control is meant to distrust.
findings.failure_mode: Failure: the second Explore appends its rows incrementally and writes {id: bd-x, agree: true} on a first look, then {id: bd-x, agree: false, evidence: 'fix never landed'} after re-checking. --check reads only the first row and reports all sampled closures confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject VERIFIED files with duplicate ids (`jq -r .id | sort | uniq -d`), and require a boolean with `jq -e '.agree == true' <<<"$v"`.
findings.failure_scenario: Failure: the second Explore appends its rows incrementally and writes {id: bd-x, agree: true} on a first look, then {id: bd-x, agree: false, evidence: 'fix never landed'} after re-checking. --check reads only the first row and reports all sampled closures confirmed.
